sources.entry: Docuseal - Create, fill, and sign digital documents (alternative to DocuSign). (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker
DocuSeal | Create, fill and sign digital documents

summary.one_liner: DocuSeal is an open source platform for creating PDF forms, filling them, and signing them online from any device.
summary.what_it_does: DocuSeal provides a WYSIWYG PDF form field builder with 12 field types, including signature, date, file, and checkbox fields. Multiple submitters can complete one document, and the README lists automated emails via SMTP and automatic PDF eSignature with signature verification. Files can be stored on disk or on AWS S3, Google Storage, or Azure Cloud. It includes user management, a mobile-optimized web interface in 7 UI languages with signing in 14 languages, and an API with webhooks for integrations. The README says it can be deployed in minutes, with Docker, Docker Compose, and several one-click hosting options. Pro features listed in the README include bulk send from CSV/XLSX, SSO/SAML, conditional fields, SMS identity verification, and embedded signing and form builder components.
use_cases: Collect signatures on PDF contracts online
Fill and sign forms from a phone
Self-host an e-signing service instead of DocuSign
Send documents to multiple signers in turn
Integrate document signing into a web or mobile app via API
Store signed documents on S3 or Azure
stack: Caddy (used with Docker Compose for SSL)
notable: Alternative to DocuSign for self-hosted e-signing
Supports SQLite by default, or PostgreSQL/MySQL via DATABASE_URL
Automatic SSL with Caddy under a custom domain in the Compose setup
Embedded signing and form builder components for React, Vue, Angular, or JavaScript (Pro)
caveats: Many features (bulk send, SSO/SAML, SMS verification, reminders, embedded components, white-label) are listed as Pro features
README describes a commercial services offering (integration consulting) alongside the open source project
